title: The midday law and the prophets before the coming of the only Son
english: for truly our God, the true light, enlightened humanity through the commandments of the law. For "the commandment of the Lord is clear, and it gives light to the eyes" (Psalms 19:8). And again, "your ordinances are light."

From the sixth hour begins the second half of the day. For the years from the beginning of creation to its fulfillment had reached their midpoint. Then Moses and Aaron were sent at midday. Worship under the law lasted until the eighth hour. The ninth hour is the time of the Spirit-bearing prophets. They too were sent as good laborers by the landowner to work the vineyard of our soul. They worked until the tenth hour.

The eleventh hour is the coming of the only Son. For in the last days, at the fulfillment of the ages, the Son of God came to us, the Word of God. As one last hour runs from the eleventh to the twelfth, so one hour runs from the coming of Christ to the fulfillment.

orientation: Cyril is still counting the hours of the parable, moving from the time of the law through the prophets to the coming of Christ as the eleventh hour.

title: The idle Gentiles hired at the eleventh hour
english: Listen to John when he says, “Little children, it is the last hour” (1 John 2:18). You see that when the master of the vineyard went out at the eleventh hour, he found idle people and hired them. Who are these idle people? We are—we who come from the Gentiles. For we were idle from the knowledge of God, idle from good works. And he says to them, “Why have you been standing here idle all day?” “All day” signified the whole span of time from the beginning of the creation of the world until his coming. For until then the Gentiles were idle, not knowing God. “No one,” they say, “has hired us.” The Gentiles are reasonable in saying this, for no one had hired them—no laws, no prophets. Those were sent to Israel, not to the Gentiles. That is why they rightly say, “No one has hired us.” But the landowner is good, for he says, “You also go and work in the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.”

title: The Idle Become Laborers and Are Paid Equally
english: The idle have now become laborers. This Church was once idle, but she works now. The band of the apostles, martyrs, ascetics, those living as monks, holy virgins, those with self control, and those in honorable marriage is at work. This Church has received the one denarius worthily.
A worker who labors swiftly can present in one hour as much work as one who has labored since early morning. In a single hour the thief heard, “Today you will be with me in paradise” (Luke 23:43).

But hear what those earlier laborers say: “We bore the burden and the heat of the day” (Matthew 20:12). They speak the truth. For they did not bear under the law the burden of the yoke of the law, but these others became equal to them through the work. So the landowner says, “Fellow, I do you no wrong” (Matthew 20:13). The judge of righteousness does no wrong. He adds that he wishes to grant favor to this one.
